legend: At the Latin America ICPC Championship 2026, the problemsetter's team ran into a tricky problem. One of the members on the team, Avnith immediately recognized the problem and claimed that it is trivially solved by [REDACTED]. However, the problem was actually solved by Centroid Decomposition and NTT. During the flight back from Chile, the problemsetter could not forget about the incident and made a problem based on [REDACTED]. Now it is your job to figure out what [REDACTED] is and solve the problem.
You are given an undirected tree with n%%ZSMJ0%% vertices and an integer k%%ZSMJ1%%.

For every vertex r%%ZSMJ2%% considered as the root, define dr(v)%%ZSMJ3%% to be the distance from r%%ZSMJ4%% to v%%ZSMJ5%%. For every k%%ZSMJ6%%-vertex subset S%%ZSMJ7%%, let lcar(S)%%ZSMJ8%% be the lowest common ancestor of all vertices in S%%ZSMJ9%% in the tree rooted at r%%ZSMJ10%%.
Let f(r)=∑S∈V|S|=kdr(lcar(S))%%ZSMJ11%% In other words, the sum of the depths of the least common ancestor of all sets with k%%ZSMJ12%% vertices if the tree is rooted at vertex r%%ZSMJ13%%.
Find f(r)%%ZSMJ14%% for each r%%ZSMJ15%% from 1%%ZSMJ16%% to n%%ZSMJ17%%. Since the answers may be large, output them modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ18%%.
input: The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ19%%, k%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤n,k≤2⋅105)%%ZSMJ21%% as denoted in the problem statement.
The next n−1%%ZSMJ22%% lines contain two integers each line, denoting an edge in the tree.
Tests in subtasks are numbered from 1−25%%ZSMJ23%% with samples skipped. Each test is worth 10025=4%%ZSMJ24%% points.
output: One line with n%%ZSMJ30%% integers; the i%%ZSMJ31%%-th integer denotes f(i)%%ZSMJ32%% modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ33%%.
note: Consider rooting at r=1%%ZSMJ34%%. The tree is a path 1−2−3−4%%ZSMJ35%%, so the depths are d1(1)=0%%ZSMJ36%%, d1(2)=1%%ZSMJ37%%, d1(3)=2%%ZSMJ38%%, d1(4)=3%%ZSMJ39%%. There are \binom{4}{2} = 6%%ZSMJ40%% subsets of size k = 2%%ZSMJ41%%:
